     6  module

    10  /-! # Local properties of processes
    11  
    12  This file defines local and stable properties of stochastic processes with respect to a filtration.
    13  This is notably useful for local martingales.
    14  
    15  ## Main definitions
    16  
    17  * `IsPreLocalizingSequence`: A pre-localizing sequence is a sequence of stopping
    18    times which tends almost surely to infinity.
    19  * `IsLocalizingSequence`: A localizing sequence is a pre-localizing sequence
    20    which is almost surely non-decreasing.
    21  * `Locally`: A stochastic process `X` is said to satisfy a property `p` locally
    22    with respect to a filtration `𝓕` if there exists a localizing sequence `(τ n)` such that for all
    23    `n`, the stopped process `X^{τ n} I_{τ n > ⊥}` satisfies `p`.
    24  * `IsStable`: A property of stochastic processes is said to be stable if it is
    25    preserved under taking the stopped process `X^{τ} I_{τ > ⊥}` by a stopping time `τ`.
    26  
    27  ## Main results
    28  
    29  * `IsStable.isStable_locally`: If a property `p` is stable, then the property
    30    "satisfies `p` locally" is also stable.
    31  * `IsPreLocalizingSequence.isLocalizingSequence_biInf`: Given a
    32    pre-localizing sequence `(τ n)`, the sequence `⊓ j ≥ n, τ j` is a localizing sequence.
    33  * `IsStable.locally_of_isPreLocalizingSequence`: If a property `p` is stable, then
    34    to prove that `X` satisfies `p` locally, one can replace the localizing sequence in the definition
    35    of "locally" by a pre-localizing sequence.
    36  * `IsStable.locally_locally`: For stable properties, locally is idempotent.
    37  * `IsStable.locally_induction`: If `q` is a stable property, and `p` implies
    38    locally `q`, then locally `p` implies locally `q`.
    39  
    40  ### Tags
    41  
    42  localizing sequence, local property, stable property
    43  -/

    48  open scoped ENNReal Topology

    50  namespace ProbabilityTheory
    51  
    52  variable {ι Ω E : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}

    54  /-- A pre-localizing sequence is a sequence of stopping times that tends almost surely to

    60    tendsto_top : ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, Tendsto (τ · ω) atTop (𝓝 ⊤)
    61  
    62  /-- A localizing sequence is a sequence of stopping times that is almost surely increasing and
    63  tends almost surely to infinity. -/
    64  structure IsLocalizingSequence [Preorder ι] [TopologicalSpace ι] [OrderTopology ι]
    65      (𝓕 : Filtration ι mΩ) (τ : ℕ → Ω → WithTop ι)
    66      (P : Measure Ω := by volume_tac) extends IsPreLocalizingSequence 𝓕 τ P where
    67    mono : ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, Monotone (τ · ω)
    68

    11  /-!
    12  # Hitting times
    13  
    14  Given a stochastic process, the hitting time provides the first time the process "hits" some
    15  subset of the state space. The hitting time is a stopping time in the case that the time index is
    16  discrete and the process is strongly adapted (this is true in a far more general setting however
    17  we have only proved it for the discrete case so far).
    18  
    19  ## Main definition
    20  
    21  * `MeasureTheory.hittingBtwn u s n m`: the first time a stochastic process `u` enters a set `s`
    22    after time `n` and before time `m`
    23  * `MeasureTheory.hittingAfter u s n`: the first time a stochastic process `u` enters a set `s`
    24    after time `n`
    25  
    26  ## Main results
    27  
    28  * `MeasureTheory.Adapted.isStoppingTime_hittingBtwn`: a discrete hitting time of an adapted process
    29    is a stopping time
    30  * `MeasureTheory.Adapted.isStoppingTime_hittingAfter`: a discrete hitting time of a adapted process
    31    is a stopping time
    32  
    33  -/

    51  /-- Hitting time: given a stochastic process `u` and a set `s`, `hittingBtwn u s n m` is
    52  the first time `u` is in `s` after time `n` and before time `m` (if `u` does not hit `s`
    53  after time `n` and before `m` then the hitting time is simply `m`).
    54  
    55  The hitting time is a stopping time if the process is strongly adapted and discrete. -/
    56  noncomputable def hittingBtwn (u : ι → Ω → β)
    57      (s : Set β) (n m : ι) : Ω → ι :=
    58    fun x => if ∃ j ∈ Set.Icc n m, u j x ∈ s
    59      then sInf (Set.Icc n m ∩ {i : ι | u i x ∈ s}) else m
    60  
    61  open scoped Classical in
    62  /-- Hitting time: given a stochastic process `u` and a set `s`, `hittingAfter u s n` is
    63  the first time `u` is in `s` after time `n` (if `u` does not hit `s` after time `n` then the
    64  hitting time is `⊤`). -/
    65  noncomputable def hittingAfter (u : ι → Ω → β) (s : Set β) (n : ι) :
    66      Ω → WithTop ι :=
    67    fun x ↦ if ∃ j, n ≤ j ∧ u j x ∈ s then (sInf {i : ι | n ≤ i ∧ u i x ∈ s} : ι) else ⊤
